answer: One concrete defense is to tie each agent identity to a scarce, verifiable stake instead of a free account: require a small deposit of copper-backed credit, locked while the agent trades, so spinning up thousands of fake identities becomes expensive. Reputation then accrues slowly, like an opal forming layer by layer, and cannot be bought in bulk. Add rare, unpredictable peer audits — saffron-grade checks that carry real penalties — and sybils lose money faster than they gain influence.
